title: feat(service-record-context): cap the body outline's entries and state the cut
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-support-ai"} -->
_Requested by **Yibo Wang** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01BVUyyPie8gHwoPM18iABwB?thread=cmsg_01BVUyyPie8gHwoPM18iABwBEaJzgBWzjWCNjBjkVoeRto)_

repo:objectstack#3 · os-support-ai · session_01WGufzi13yZRqVcp2mGonWK

Fixes #37178

Clause-②: yes (widening)
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读
- 用户能看到什么变化：AI 代理读取一条正文很长、几乎全是标题的记录时，拿到的目录最多列 80 条，超出时多一句说明有多少个标题没列出；以前目录没有上限，可能和正文一样大。
- 为什么做：属于“按记录向 AI 提问”这一大项，补上目录不设上限、让正文 8000 字上限形同虚设的口子。
- 出错会怎样：受影响的只有读超长正文的 AI 代理，最坏是目录少列了标题，没列出的章节仍能按锚点读到；纯服务端改动，可直接撤回。
- 要你做什么：无。

## What changes

`get_record_context` answers a long body with an outline of its headings. The outline had no cap: a long body that is almost all headings made an outline as big as the body, which undid the 8000-character body bound. The outline is now bounded whatever the body holds.

- **`RECORD_CONTEXT_OUTLINE_MAX_ENTRIES = 80`**, a service constant beside `RECORD_CONTEXT_BODY_MAX_CHARS` (exported from the package index). An outline lists at most 80 headings, AND its listing, serialized, stays within `RECORD_CONTEXT_BODY_MAX_CHARS`. The entry cap alone does not meet the card's acceptance ("bounded by the constant, whatever the body holds"): a heading's text, and the anchor derived from it, is as long as the author makes it, so 80 entries of 5,000-character headings would still be an unbounded answer. The character bound closes that; it reuses the body bound instead of coining a third number.
- **Which headings a cut keeps** (`boundedOutline` in `body-outline.ts`): headings are admitted shallowest level first, in body order within a level, until the next would pass either bound, and are listed in body order. So a cut leaves out the deepest headings first, and a listed section's text holds the headings left out under it (a section runs to the next heading of the same or a higher level). For a body of many headings at one level this is a plain prefix cut.
- **Anchors past the cap stay readable** (decided and pinned): the cap bounds the listing, not which sections exist. A section call resolves its anchor against every heading, listed or not, and anchors are numbered over every heading, so a listed anchor is the same whether or not the outline was cut.
- **One note per cut, kind `outline_truncated`** (new `RecordContextNoteKind` value, docblock updated). It sits beside `body_outline`. Its sentence, in `en` and `zh-Hans`, says how many headings are listed, how many the body has and how many are not listed. It carries no record text.
- **Edge**: a body whose first-admitted heading is too long to list within the bound (a heading over about 4,000 characters) gets no empty outline. It is carried as text up to the bound and marked `truncated`, with the `body_truncated` note, the same as a long body with no headings.
- Spec: the `outline` field's `.describe()` now says the outline is held to the service's bounds and a cut is stated by an `outline_truncated` note. The reference page is regenerated (`gen:docs`).

### Why a new note kind (Clause-② `yes`), not the existing `truncated` mark plus `body_truncated`

I checked this as the claim asked. The existing pieces cannot carry the cut honestly:
- `RecordContextBody.truncated` is described as "Present when `text` was cut at the bound". An outline cut has no `text`, so setting it there would contradict its published description.
- `body_truncated` is documented as "the body (or a section) was cut at the bound", a character cut of text. Using it for an entry cut would quietly change what a published kind means. An added enum value is visible to every consumer; a changed meaning is not.
- Neither one carries the count. The count goes in the note's sentence, as `related_truncated` carries its cap.

So the published output enum widens by one value: `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: none` (nothing an author writes changes), changesets at `patch`. Under the claim, this owes the L2 at CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER. Repo grep: no consumer switches over the note kinds exhaustively (the MCP and runtime bridges pass notes through).

### How the number was chosen

I measured the outline reader on real long documents: the 543 Markdown files of this repository (`content/docs`, `docs`, `skills`) that are past the 8000-character body bound and have headings, at a33691e5.

| reading | value |
|:--|:--|
| mean serialized size of one outline entry | 95.4 chars |
| headings per document, p50 / p90 / p95 / p99 / max | 19 / 48 / 60 / 103 / 425 |
| documents an entry cap of 40 / 60 / 80 / 100 would cut | 75 / 24 / 15 / 9 |

80 entries × about 95 chars is about 7,600 chars: an outline answer the size of the body bound, as the claim asked. With both bounds applied (`boundedOutline`), **527 of the 543 are listed uncut**, 4 of the 16 cut ones are cut by the character bound before the entry cap, none gets an empty outline, and the largest outline serializes to 7,994 chars.

## Tests

The new pins go into the package's two existing test files as top-level `describe` blocks, under the shared-harness rule in AGENTS.md: the executor pins sit beside the `fake-door` harness, and the reader pins beside the outline reader's own pins.

- `record-context-tools.test.ts`: `RECORD_CONTEXT_OUTLINE_MAX_ENTRIES` pinned at 80 in the constants block. A new block, "the outline bound", pins four things:
  - a body of 300 short headings lists exactly 80, the outline serializes within the body bound, the notes are `['body_outline', 'outline_truncated']`, and the cut note names 220 and 300 and carries no record text;
  - the cut is stated in the caller's locale (`zh-CN`);
  - the anchor of heading 300 (not listed) reads its section;
  - a body whose only heading is too long to list is carried truncated.
- `body-outline.test.ts`: a new block, "the outline is bounded whatever the body holds", pins `boundedOutline` directly:
  - within the cap, every heading is listed and none left out;
  - the entry cap is a body-order prefix at one level;
  - shallowest first: with 10 parts of 20 clauses each, all 10 parts and the first 70 clauses are listed, in body order;
  - long headings are held to the character bound before the cap;
  - a heading too long to list is left out;
  - numbered anchors are unchanged by a cut.

## Acceptance notes

- The outline's `.describe()` and the new kind's docblock are spec prose in the claimed file. They state only what this PR implements. No ADR-0160 ruling is changed: D3 says every cut is stated in the notes and the bounds are service constants pinned by test.
- Consumer side of the widened enum: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/mcp exec vitest run src/mcp-record-context-tools.test.ts` passed, 10/10. No consumer reads the note kinds exhaustively. The runtime bridge test is left to CI's Test Core.

## Verification

Read first:
1. `packages/services/service-record-context/src/body-outline.ts`, `boundedOutline`: the admission order and the two `break`s.
2. `packages/services/service-record-context/src/record-context-tools.ts`, the outline branch: the `listed` guard and the fallback to truncated text when nothing can be listed.
3. `packages/spec/src/ai/record-context-tools.zod.ts`: the new `outline_truncated` value.

Two-minute check: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-record-context exec vitest run -t "outline bound"` should show 4 tests passed, including "an unlisted heading's anchor reads its section".
